issues.description: The UML in the problem statement specifies addGuestStudents(int): void, but the solution implementation defines addGuestStudents(int) returning boolean. This mismatch between the expected return type (void) and the solution (boolean) can confuse students about the intended behavior and whether they should return a value (and what it represents). It may also cause tests or exemplar code to disagree with student implementations.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution's addGuestStudents method to have a void return type and drop the boolean return values (updating any internal logic/tests accordingly), or (B) update the problem statement/UML to indicate that addGuestStudents(int) returns a boolean and document what the boolean signifies (e.g., success/failure). Ensure the template includes the correct signature to match the chosen option.
